data_as_of: YouTube readings of 2026-10-16 and 2026-10-22; 1,433 songs first uploaded 2026-09-15 to 2026-10-15 across 6 labels
note: Written by reviewing the numbers on this page; not generated live. It does not update when the data changes. Live AI explanations and Ask Music AI come with the LLM integration.
briefing:
#### This month in one view
- **Volume is not performance.** T-Series uploaded 619 of the 1,433 songs (43%) and has the most total views (577M), but its typical song is in only the **43rd percentile** against songs of the same age. Think Music (27 songs) sits at the **85th**, Sony Music India and Saregama at the **57th**. A large share of T-Series uploads are small regional and devotional releases that pull the median down.
- **Hindi and Haryanvi lead on a like-for-like basis** (66th and 62nd percentile); **Kannada, Gujarati and Punjabi trail** (20th-31st). Telugu has the most songs (394) but a 39th-percentile median.
- **Strongest label x language pockets:** T-Series Haryanvi (91st percentile, 10 songs), Think Music Tamil and Telugu (85th-87th), Zee Gujarati (85th), T-Series Bengali (84th). **Weakest:** T-Series Tamil and Marathi (14th), Zee Tamil (18th), T-Series Telugu (25th, despite 149M views from a few big films).
- **Older songs are a real lever:** 452 songs (32%) were first released a year or more before their current upload, and several are among the fastest of the month, e.g. [Nagada Sang Dhol](#song:151) (2013) and [Lallati Bhandar](#song:101) (2013).
- **Watch engagement, not just views:** 20 of the 300 fastest songs get under 1 like per 1,000 views (typical is about 6). Six of the eight lowest are Zee Music Company releases. Very low engagement on fast-rising videos is often a sign of paid promotion; public data can't confirm that.

#### What the data can't tell yet
Only 2 days of daily readings exist (16 and 22 Oct). Growth, acceleration and anomaly signals become reliable after about a week of daily readings, so today's rankings lean on age-adjusted views per day.

panels.emerging:
#### Key findings
- The strongest rising songs not yet in the top 5% are **8-17 days old** and adding **190,000-390,000 views a day**, faster than 94-97% of songs their age: [Awadhiya Ke Raja](#song:1438) (Zee, Hindi devotional), [Those Pe Badmashi](#song:1248) (T-Series, Haryanvi), [Humsafar](#song:684) (Saregama, Hindi), [Abar Elo Maa](#song:1218) (T-Series, Bengali), [Chitta Kukkad](#song:1342) (T-Series, Punjabi).
- **Regional and devotional songs dominate the list:** Haryanvi, Bhojpuri, Bengali, Punjabi and Navratri devotional songs ([Godiya Me Balakawa](#song:1247), [Maa Ka Saja Hai Darbar](#song:1241)) sit next to film songs like [Jim Jim Tara](#song:237) (Aditya, Telugu) and [Tiger Siva](#song:233) (Saregama, Tamil).
- **Engagement separates organic from pushed growth:** [Those Pe Badmashi](#song:1248) (10 likes per 1,000 views) and [4 Khapeetar](#song:541) (10.2) pair speed with strong engagement; [Awadhiya Ke Raja](#song:1438) (0.6) and [Dhoop](#song:1366) (0.4) are fast but get very few likes for their views, which can point to promoted views (a hypothesis).

#### Watch out
- Every score here is an **early signal** (age-adjusted speed only): these songs have one daily reading so far. Breakout scores will separate songs that keep accelerating from launch spikes after a few more daily syncs.
- One entry is named "Tulsi Kumar" because the video title starts with the singer's name; its real song name needs a naming fix.

#### Suggested actions
- Re-check this list after 3-4 daily syncs and act on songs whose growth holds or accelerates.
- For songs with high speed and high engagement (e.g. Those Pe Badmashi), consider Shorts, playlist pitching and regional promotion while momentum is building.
panels.cross_label:
#### Key findings
- **Age-adjusted ranking of labels** (median percentile of their songs against songs of the same age): Think Music 85, Sony Music India 57, Saregama 57, Aditya Music 48, Zee Music Company 46, T-Series 43.
- **T-Series wins on volume, not consistency:** 577M views from 619 songs, but only 45% of its songs beat a typical song of the same age. Its strengths are concentrated: **Haryanvi (91st percentile)**, Rajasthani (85th), Bengali (84th) and Hindi (70th, 154 songs); Tamil, Marathi (both 14th) and Telugu (25th) pull it down.
- **Think Music is small but consistent:** 26 of its 27 songs beat a typical song of their age, in both Tamil and Telugu.
- **Saregama's best pockets** are Kannada (78th) and Bhojpuri (71st); its Punjabi (18th), Gujarati (25th) and Malayalam (28th) releases underperform.
- **Zee Music Company** does well in Gujarati (85th) and Hindi (67th) but is weak in Malayalam (20th) and Tamil (18th).
- **Language view:** Hindi (66th) and Haryanvi (62nd) over-perform; Kannada (20th), Gujarati (28th) and Punjabi (31st) under-perform. Odia and Gujarati audiences engage most (12.8 and 9.9 likes per 1,000 views) despite low reach.

#### Watch out
- Groups with 5-10 songs (e.g. Rajasthani, Think Music Telugu) can swing with one release.
- Language is derived by rules (title words, YouTube audio language, channel); a few songs may be misclassified.

#### Suggested actions
- Benchmark each label inside its own language pockets, not on totals.
- Treat Haryanvi, Bhojpuri and Hindi independent releases as growth pockets; review release strategy for Tamil and Marathi at T-Series and Malayalam at Zee and Saregama.
panels.catalog:
#### Key findings
- **452 of 1,433 songs (32%)** were first released a year or more before their current upload, so re-uploads and new videos of older songs are a large part of every label's output.
- Several older songs run faster than 85-98% of new uploads their age: [Virisina](#song:462) (Aditya, 2022 film *Raajahyogam*, 604,000 views/day), [Nagada Sang Dhol](#song:151) (Sony, 2013, 409,000/day), [Lallati Bhandar](#song:101) (Sony, Marathi, 2013, 185,000/day), [Nit Khair Manga](#song:1023) (T-Series, 2018), [Ramuloo Ramulaa](#song:274) (Aditya, 2019) and [Aakasam Enatido](#song:496) (Aditya, 1982 film *Nereekshana*).
- **Festive timing shows:** Nagada Sang Dhol, Lallati Bhandar and [Dhol Bajaa](#song:140) are Navratri and garba favourites, re-released in the festival weeks.

#### Watch out
- "First released" comes from Spotify, Apple Music or MusicBrainz and can be a compilation date rather than the original release.
- Speed here measures the new upload only, not the song's older videos elsewhere.

#### Suggested actions
- Plan festival re-releases (high-quality 8K and lyric versions) about two weeks before Navratri, Ganesh Chaturthi and Durga Puja.
- Use the fastest catalogue songs as anchors for playlists and Shorts to lift related newer releases.
panels.artists:singer:
#### Key findings
- Of the 60 singers with 3+ songs this month, **14 are consistent** (most songs above typical, no single song over half their views), **23 are one-hit dependent** (one song brings 70%+ of their views) and 23 are mixed.
- **Broad-based performers:** Hiphop Tamizha (4 songs, all above typical, top song 42% of views), Anmol Salh, Swara Verma and Mangli (5 songs across 4 labels, 80% above typical).
- **Vishal Mishra** is the busiest high performer: 11 songs across Saregama, T-Series and Zee, every one above typical (median 94th percentile).
- **One-hit dependent despite big totals:** Ajay Gogavale (95% of views from *Endhayya Saami*), Siddharth Basrur (94% from *Vingansa*), B Praak (93%), Sai Abhyankkar (75% from *Ooroda Oththa Don*).
- Shreya Ghoshal has the most songs (16) but a 72nd-percentile median: steady rather than spiky.

#### Watch out
- Credits come from video descriptions; spellings vary (e.g. Sublashini / Sublahshini count as two singers).

#### Suggested actions
- Pitch consistent performers (Vishal Mishra, Hiphop Tamizha, Mangli) for new releases where predictable performance matters.
- For one-hit artists, test follow-up releases soon after the hit to convert attention into a catalogue.
panels.artists:music_director:
#### Key findings
- **Consistent composers** with many songs: Rochak Kohli (13 songs, top song only 25% of views, 93rd percentile), Anirudh Ravichander (21 songs, top 29%), Ajay-Atul (17 songs), Ravi Basrur and Hiphop Tamizha (4 songs each, all above typical).
- **One-hit dependent:** Tanishk Bagchi (94% of views from *Thummak Thummak*) and Sai Abhyankkar (75% from *Ooroda Oththa Don*).
- Rochak Kohli works across Saregama, Sony and T-Series in the same month: the strongest cross-label composer by consistency.

#### Watch out
- "Ajay" and "Atul" also appear separately from "Ajay-Atul" because some descriptions write the duo as "Ajay - Atul"; their numbers overlap.

#### Suggested actions
- Use composer consistency as a release-planning input: pair breakout singers with consistent composers.
- Fix the duo-name split before using composer rankings externally.
panels.anomalies:
#### Key findings
- Only **56 songs**, all from Sony Music India, have the three readings needed to measure a change in growth, because Sony was the only label tracked on 16 Oct. The list is a preview, not a market view.
- The large "spikes" ([Pesamale](#song:271) 259x, [Kalyana Virundhu](#song:209) 19x) compare a few-hour gap on 16 Oct with the 6-day gap to 22 Oct, so they overstate the change. Treat them as "needs a second look", not as confirmed spikes.
- The "drops" (e.g. [Kya Khoya](#song:145), [The Naari Naari Song](#song:150), 8-14 days old) are the normal slowdown after a launch week, not problems.

#### Watch out
- Anomalies need evenly spaced daily readings. With daily syncs running, this panel becomes meaningful in about a week and will cover every label.

#### Suggested actions
- Keep the daily pipeline running without gaps; review this panel weekly once 7+ days of readings exist.
